predecessors.name: Lê dynasty
predecessors.text: the whole Lê realm of 1527: Cliopatria's 1529 outline without Phú Yên and Khánh Hòa

successors.name: Trịnh lords
successors.text: Cao Bằng province, where the Mạc survived to 1677 as a rump state under Ming and Qing protection

ledger.x: 15 June 1527: Mạc Đăng Dung proclaims the Mạc dynasty.
1540: Mạc Đăng Dung submits to the Ming and cedes land.
1554: the Lê regain the far south.
September 1559: the Lê-Trịnh army marches north.
1573: the Mạc retake Thăng Long, 'a year later'.
1592: the Mạc court withdraws to Cao Bằng (infobox 'Cao Bằng (1592-1677)'; Mạc Kính Cung ruled there 1593-1625).
February 1592: the Southern court launches its last offensive.
1592: the Mạc lose Đông Kinh and the north.
April 1593: the Lê emperor returns to Đông Kinh.

wars.name: Lê-Mạc War
wars.outcome: The Revival Lê dynasty wins: it recovers the south by 1533-1554, Đông Kinh in 1592 and, through the Trịnh, Cao Bằng in 1677; the Mạc rump survives in Cao Bằng under Ming and Qing support.

wars.name: Ming intervention against the Mạc
wars.outcome: The Jiajing Emperor sends 125,000 soldiers to the border in 1537 at the Lê request (Lê-Mạc War page) and threatens 110,000 men from Guangxi; Mạc Đăng Dung submits in 1540, cedes land and is downgraded to a governor, and the Ming accept him as ruler of part of…

wars.name: Lê attack on Cao Bằng (1627)
wars.outcome: Mạc Kính Khoan surrenders and accepts the Lê title Thông quốc công; the Mạc nevertheless hold Cao Bằng to 1677 (the page is silent on 1627-1638).

wars.name: Qing mediation over Cao Bằng and the Trịnh conquest
wars.outcome: The Kangxi Emperor demands in 1667 that Trịnh Tạc return Cao Bằng to the Mạc, loses interest by 1673; the Trịnh defeat the Mạc in 1677 and Mạc Kính Vũ flees to Guangxi.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages: the Ming-Mạc frontier of 1540 is a cession of 'land' without a boundary, the Lê-Mạc front moved by campaign, and Cliopatria's outlines are 16-km cells.
